source: Adapted from the Focus30 design (student self-help app, Oct 2026), rewritten for Four.

checkin.title: Study check-in
checkin.intro: 14 quick questions. Think about the last two weeks. There are no right or wrong answers. This is not a test.

items.text: When I study, my mind wanders after a few minutes.
I can stay on one task for 25 minutes.
I start homework at the last moment.
When a task feels big, I avoid it.
After I put something off, I am very hard on myself.
I feel there is too much to do.
Before tests, worry makes it hard to think.
I go to bed at very different times.
I use a phone or screen just before sleep.
I check my phone while studying, without planning to.
I lose track of time on videos or chats.
I can see how school links to things I care about.
It is hard to get going, even on things I want to do.

profiles.name: The Busy Planner
profiles.tagline: You care a lot. The to-do list feels too big.
profiles.about: You see everything you must do. So starting feels heavy. Your plan makes tasks small and calms your mind.
watch: Waiting to feel calm before you start
Being hard on yourself after a delay
profiles.tip: Pick one task. Write its first 5-minute step on paper.

profiles.name: The Night Scroller
profiles.tagline: Your phone keeps you up at night.
profiles.about: Late-night phone time is very common. Apps are made to be hard to put down. Your plan protects your sleep with small changes.
profiles.tip: Tonight, charge your phone where you cannot reach it from bed.

profiles.name: The Multitasker
profiles.tagline: Chats open, videos playing, homework waiting.
profiles.about: You are quick and like variety. But jumping between things tires your focus. Your plan gives you short times with one task only.
profiles.tip: Do one 25-minute study time. Put your phone in another room.

profiles.name: The Last-Minute Runner
profiles.tagline: You finish at the last moment. It costs you.
profiles.about: Deadlines wake you up. You can finish under pressure. But rushing every time is stressful. Your plan helps you start earlier.
watch: "I will start when I feel like it"
Thinking tasks take less time than they do
profiles.tip: Set your own deadline two days before the real one. Tell someone.

profiles.name: The Juggler
profiles.tagline: So much to carry. Little time to breathe.
profiles.about: You carry a lot. Stress means your body is working hard. It does not mean you are failing. Your plan teaches quick ways to calm down.
strengths: You keep going when it is hard
profiles.tip: Before you study, breathe slowly for two minutes.

profiles.name: The Wanderer
profiles.tagline: Your mind loves to explore, even while you study.
profiles.about: You are curious. Your mind jumps to new ideas. Your plan helps you park those ideas and come back to the task.
profiles.tip: Keep a "later" list next to you. Write stray thoughts there.

profiles.name: The Night Owl
profiles.tagline: You wake up late at night. Mornings are hard.
profiles.about: Your energy comes late. But school starts early. Your plan helps you move your body clock with small steps.
strengths: You have energy in the evening
profiles.tip: Pick one wake-up time. Keep it every day, even Sunday.

profiles.name: The Phone Magnet
profiles.about: Phones are made to grab you. That is not your fault. Your plan helps you use your phone when you choose.
strengths: You know what is going on
watch: Phone next to you while studying
profiles.tip: Turn off sounds for every app except real people.

profiles.name: The Spark Seeker
profiles.tagline: You are looking for a reason that makes it click.
profiles.about: Studying feels hard when you do not see why. Your plan helps you find your reason and get small wins.
strengths: You can work hard for things you care about
watch: Giving up after one bad day
profiles.tip: Write one sentence: how can a subject help you or your family?

profiles.name: The Steady Builder
profiles.tagline: You have good habits. You are ready to grow.
profiles.about: Things are going well for you. Your plan keeps your habits strong in busy weeks, like exam time.
profiles.tip: Pick one habit to protect in your next busy week.

plan.intro: One short lesson and one tiny action a day. About 5 minutes. Missed a day? Just carry on.

reflect.title: Week {w}: look back
reflect.text: Take 5 minutes. What worked this week? Keep doing it.

prompts.text: One thing to try next week:

recheck.title: Day 30: see how far you came
recheck.text: You made it! Take the same check-in again. Compare it with Day 1. Any change counts.

focus.title: Focus is like a muscle
focus.text: Focus gets tired. It also grows with practice. Everyone's mind wanders. Noticing it is the first skill.
focus.action: Study for 10 minutes. Make a mark each time your mind wanders.
focus.why: Keeping track of your progress helps you reach your goal.

focus.title: One task at a time
focus.text: Jumping between tasks wastes energy. Clear everything else away before you start.
focus.action: Before you study, clear your desk. Write your one task on paper.
focus.why: A phone close by steals some attention, even when silent.

focus.title: The 25-5 timer
focus.text: Study 25 minutes. Rest 5 minutes. Short blocks keep you sharp.
focus.action: Do one 25-minute study block. Then rest 5 minutes.
focus.why: Short study times with planned breaks keep your mind fresh.

focus.title: Make breaks real breaks
focus.text: A phone break often grows to 40 minutes. Real breaks are short and calm.
focus.action: Write three breaks with no phone. Use one today.
focus.why: Short study times with planned breaks keep your mind fresh.

focus.title: The "later" list
focus.text: Random thoughts pull you off task. Write them down. Then let them go.
focus.action: Keep a "later" list next to you while you study.
focus.why: A clear "when… then…" plan makes you far more likely to act.

focus.title: Pick a study spot
focus.text: Places can switch your brain to study mode. A bed says "rest".
focus.action: Choose one study spot. Use it all week.
focus.why: Same time, same place, every day: that is how habits grow.

focus.title: Start with a finish line
focus.text: "Study maths" is too vague. "Do 10 questions" is clear.
focus.action: Before you study, finish this: "By the end, I will…"
focus.why: Small, clear steps are easier to start. Each one done gives you hope.

focus.title: Plan for distractions
focus.text: Decide before: "If I want my phone, I write it down instead."
focus.action: Write two "if… then…" plans. Put them where you study.
focus.why: A clear "when… then…" plan makes you far more likely to act.

focus.title: Test yourself
focus.text: Reading again feels good but teaches little. Close the book and remember.
focus.action: After reading, close the book. Write three things you remember.
focus.why: Testing yourself, a few days apart, is a top way to learn.

focus.title: Little and often
focus.text: Short study times over days beat one long night.
focus.action: Plan two short reviews of today's topic in the next 3 days.
focus.why: Testing yourself, a few days apart, is a top way to learn.

focus.title: Your best hours
focus.text: Focus is easier at some times of day. Do hard work then.
focus.action: Rate your focus from 1 to 5: morning, afternoon, evening.
focus.why: Keeping track of your progress helps you reach your goal.

focus.title: Two blocks in a row
focus.text: One block is easy now. Try two with a longer break.
focus.action: Do two 25-minute blocks. Rest 10 minutes between them.
focus.why: Short study times with planned breaks keep your mind fresh.

focus.title: Quiet or music?
focus.text: Songs with words can fight with reading. Test what works for you.
focus.action: Study once in quiet, once with soft music. Rate each 1 to 5.
focus.why: Keeping track of your progress helps you reach your goal.

focus.title: Move to reset
focus.text: When focus fades, a short walk brings it back.
focus.action: Between study blocks, walk or stretch for 3 minutes.
focus.why: Moving your body helps sleep and lowers worry.

focus.title: Start with the easy part
focus.text: Starting is the hardest part. An easy start gets you moving.
focus.action: Start with 5 minutes on the easiest part.
focus.why: Small, clear steps are easier to start. Each one done gives you hope.

focus.title: Messages at set times
focus.text: Replying all day breaks your focus. Pick two times for messages.
focus.action: Choose two times today for messages. Ignore them otherwise.
focus.why: A phone close by steals some attention, even when silent.

focus.title: Focus in class
focus.text: Write notes in your own words. Write your questions too.
focus.action: In one class, write three notes in your words and one question.
focus.why: Testing yourself, a few days apart, is a top way to learn.

focus.title: When focus falls apart
focus.text: Bad sessions happen. Stand up. Breathe three times. Start a 10-minute timer.
focus.action: Next time you lose focus: stand, breathe, set 10 minutes.
focus.why: Students who forgave themselves put things off less next time.

focus.title: Plan your week
focus.text: Put study times in your week like class times.
focus.action: Write three study times for this week in your planner.
focus.why: Short study times with planned breaks keep your mind fresh.

focus.title: Teach it back
focus.text: Explain a topic out loud, like a teacher. You see what you really know.
focus.action: Explain one thing you learned for 2 minutes, out loud.
focus.why: Testing yourself, a few days apart, is a top way to learn.

focus.title: Study groups that work
focus.text: Groups can help or waste time. A goal and a timer keep it useful.
focus.action: With friends, agree on a goal and 25 minutes before chatting.
focus.why: Short study times with planned breaks keep your mind fresh.

focus.title: Protect study time
focus.text: Tell your family when you study. Put your phone on silent.
focus.action: Put your phone on silent for one study block. Tell someone.
focus.why: A phone close by steals some attention, even when silent.

focus.title: Look at your progress
focus.text: Compare with Day 1. Small progress counts.
focus.action: Study 10 minutes and mark each wander again. Compare with Day 1.
focus.why: Keeping track of your progress helps you reach your goal.

focus.title: Your focus tools
focus.text: You tried many tools. Keep the three that helped most.
focus.action: Write your top three focus tools in your notebook.
focus.why: Same time, same place, every day: that is how habits grow.

focus.title: After Day 30
focus.text: Habits keep growing for weeks. Plans help them last.
focus.action: Write three "if… then…" plans for next month.
focus.why: A clear "when… then…" plan makes you far more likely to act.

procrastination.title: It is not laziness
procrastination.text: We put things off to escape a bad feeling. Bored? Confused? Scared? Name it.
procrastination.action: Pick one task you avoid. Name the feeling behind it.
procrastination.why: We put things off to escape a bad feeling. It is not laziness.

procrastination.title: Make the first step tiny
procrastination.text: "Do the project" is too big. "Write the title" is easy.
procrastination.action: Write a first step under 5 minutes. Do it now.
procrastination.why: Small, clear steps are easier to start. Each one done gives you hope.

procrastination.title: Just 10 minutes
procrastination.text: Promise only 10 minutes. Once you start, going on is easier.
procrastination.action: Set 10 minutes on a task you avoid. You may stop after.
procrastination.why: Short study times with planned breaks keep your mind fresh.

procrastination.title: Start at a set time
procrastination.text: "At 4 pm, after tea, I open my notes." No deciding needed.
procrastination.action: Write when and where you will start tomorrow's task.
procrastination.why: A clear "when… then…" plan makes you far more likely to act.

procrastination.title: Forgive yesterday
procrastination.text: Being hard on yourself adds another bad feeling. Be kind instead.
procrastination.action: Write one kind sentence about a task you delayed.
procrastination.why: Students who forgave themselves put things off less next time.

procrastination.title: Break a big task up
procrastination.text: One big task is scary. Five small steps with dates are not.
procrastination.action: Split one big task into five steps. Give each a day.
procrastination.why: Small, clear steps are easier to start. Each one done gives you hope.

procrastination.title: Write it down
procrastination.text: Tasks in your head are easy to dodge. Paper makes them real.
procrastination.action: Write your next three tasks with a time for each.
procrastination.why: A clear "when… then…" plan makes you far more likely to act.

procrastination.title: "I will start when I feel ready"
procrastination.text: The ready feeling comes after you start, not before.
procrastination.action: Write one delaying thought. Write a fairer one next to it.
procrastination.why: Checking a bad thought and finding a fairer one helps you.

procrastination.title: Get ready the night before
procrastination.text: Looking for a pen or notes becomes a reason to wait.
procrastination.action: Tonight, put out everything for tomorrow's first task.
procrastination.why: A clear "when… then…" plan makes you far more likely to act.

procrastination.title: Reward after, not instead
procrastination.text: A small treat after studying teaches your brain that starting pays.
procrastination.action: Pick a small treat. Have it only after one study block.
procrastination.why: Pairing a dull task with something you enjoy makes it easier to do.

procrastination.title: Start messy
procrastination.text: Wanting it perfect stops you starting. A first try can be messy.
procrastination.action: Spend 10 minutes on a rough first try. Messy is fine.
procrastination.why: Students who forgave themselves put things off less next time.

procrastination.title: Set your own deadlines
procrastination.text: Small deadlines before the real one stop the last-minute rush.
procrastination.action: Set two small deadlines before your next test or homework.
procrastination.why: Students who set their own small deadlines did better.

procrastination.title: Wish, picture, problem, plan
procrastination.text: Picture your goal. Picture what may stop you. Plan for it.
procrastination.action: For one goal, write: wish, best result, problem, plan.
procrastination.why: Thinking about the problem before it comes helps you beat it. It was tested with high school students.

procrastination.title: Busy but not studying
procrastination.text: Tidying your desk can be a way to avoid the real task.
procrastination.action: Notice today if you do "useful" things to avoid studying.
procrastination.why: Keeping track of your progress helps you reach your goal.

procrastination.title: Ask early
procrastination.text: Being confused makes us wait. Ask a teacher or friend early.
procrastination.action: Write one question about a task. Ask it today.
procrastination.why: People you can talk to make stress lighter.

procrastination.title: Tell someone your plan
procrastination.text: Saying "I start at 5" to someone helps you do it.
procrastination.action: Tell one person what you will start, and when.
procrastination.why: Students who set their own small deadlines did better.

procrastination.title: Tick it off
procrastination.text: Ticks and crossed-out steps keep you going.
procrastination.action: Tick each small step you finish today.
procrastination.why: Keeping track of your progress helps you reach your goal.

procrastination.title: Slipped? Restart today
procrastination.text: Missing a day does not wipe out your work. Start small today.
procrastination.action: Do a 5-minute restart step now.
procrastination.why: Students who forgave themselves put things off less next time.

procrastination.title: See yourself finished
procrastination.text: Picture the evening after the task is done. How does it feel?
procrastination.action: Picture finishing for 3 minutes. Write one problem and one plan.
procrastination.why: Thinking about the problem before it comes helps you beat it. It was tested with high school students.

procrastination.title: Pair the boring with the nice
procrastination.text: Do the dull task in your favourite spot, or with tea.
procrastination.action: Choose one treat you only have while studying. Use it today.
procrastination.why: Pairing a dull task with something you enjoy makes it easier to do.

procrastination.title: How long will it really take?
procrastination.text: Tasks take longer than we think. Time yourself.
procrastination.action: Guess how long one task takes. Time it. Compare.
procrastination.why: Most people think tasks take less time than they do. Timing yourself fixes this.

procrastination.title: Say no to one thing
procrastination.text: Sometimes there is just too much. Drop one small thing.
procrastination.action: Pick one thing to say no to, or move, this week.
procrastination.why: Small, clear steps are easier to start. Each one done gives you hope.

procrastination.title: Spot your pattern
procrastination.text: When and where do you put things off? Patterns show fixes.
procrastination.action: Write your top two delay times and one fix for each.
procrastination.why: Keeping track of your progress helps you reach your goal.

procrastination.title: Your start routine
procrastination.text: Join your best tools: phone away, 10-minute timer, tiny step.
procrastination.action: Write your 3-step start routine. Use it once today.
procrastination.why: Same time, same place, every day: that is how habits grow.

procrastination.title: After Day 30
procrastination.text: Plans keep your new skills going.
procrastination.action: Write three "if… then…" plans for next month.
procrastination.why: A clear "when… then…" plan makes you far more likely to act.

stress.title: Stress means "getting ready"
stress.text: A fast heart before a test is your body getting ready. It does not mean you will fail.
stress.action: When stressed, say: "My body is getting ready to help me."
stress.why: Seeing a fast heartbeat as "getting ready" helped students in exams.

stress.title: Breathe out long
stress.text: Breathe in slowly. Breathe out even longer. Your body calms down.
stress.action: Do 2 minutes of slow breathing today.
stress.why: Slow breathing with a long breath out calms your body in minutes.

stress.title: Empty your head
stress.text: Write every worry on paper. Your mind gets more space.
stress.action: Write all your worries for 5 minutes. Nobody will see it.
stress.why: Writing worries down before a test helped students get better marks.

stress.title: What can I change?
stress.text: Some worries you can change. Some you cannot. Work on the first kind.
stress.action: Draw two circles: "I can change" and "I cannot". Sort your worries.
stress.why: Checking a bad thought and finding a fairer one helps you.

stress.title: "What if everything goes wrong?"
stress.text: Stress loves the worst case. Check the facts. Find a fairer thought.
stress.action: Write one worried thought, the facts, and a fairer thought.
stress.why: Checking a bad thought and finding a fairer one helps you.

stress.title: Top three for tomorrow
stress.text: When everything feels urgent, pick just three.
stress.action: Tonight, write the three most important things for tomorrow.
stress.why: Small, clear steps are easier to start. Each one done gives you hope.

stress.title: Stress and sleep
stress.text: Stress makes sleep hard. Bad sleep makes stress bigger.
stress.action: Tonight, start calming down 30 minutes before bed.
stress.why: Regular sleep times and a calm bedtime help you sleep better.

stress.title: Move it out
stress.text: A short walk can take the edge off stress.
stress.action: Walk or play for 10 minutes today.
stress.why: Moving your body helps sleep and lowers worry.

stress.title: Talk it out
stress.text: Talking to someone you trust makes stress lighter.
stress.action: Talk to one person you trust about how things are.
stress.why: People you can talk to make stress lighter.

stress.title: Talk to yourself like a friend
stress.text: Would you call a friend "useless"? Be kind to yourself too.
stress.action: Write what you would tell a friend. Read it to yourself.
stress.why: Students who forgave themselves put things off less next time.

stress.title: Your test-nerves plan
stress.text: Before a test: write worries, breathe slowly, say "I am ready".
stress.action: Write your 3-step plan for your next test.
stress.why: Writing worries down before a test helped students get better marks.

stress.title: Plan a small joy
stress.text: Small happy moments are not wasted time. They give you energy.
stress.action: Plan one small thing you enjoy. Do it today or tomorrow.
stress.why: Noticing good things and planning small joys lifts your mood.

stress.title: A finish time for study
stress.text: Studying until you drop raises stress. Pick a time to stop.
stress.action: Choose a "study ends at" time tonight. Keep it.
stress.why: Short study times with planned breaks keep your mind fresh.

stress.title: The comparison trap
stress.text: Others show only their good side. You see all of yours.
stress.action: Notice one comparison thought. Write a fairer one.
stress.why: Checking a bad thought and finding a fairer one helps you.

stress.title: High goals, kind voice
stress.text: You can aim high and still be kind to yourself.
stress.action: Rewrite one harsh thing you told yourself. Make it kind and true.
stress.why: Students who forgave themselves put things off less next time.

stress.title: Ask for what you need
stress.text: Asking for help is a skill, not a weakness.
stress.action: Write a short message asking a teacher or friend for help.
stress.why: People you can talk to make stress lighter.

stress.title: One calm minute
stress.text: Notice your breath, the sounds, your feet on the floor.
stress.action: For 3 minutes, notice your breath and the sounds around you.
stress.why: Calm attention to the present moment lowers stress.

stress.title: Your warning signs
stress.text: A tight jaw? Snapping at people? Bad sleep? Spot stress early.
stress.action: List three stress signs. Write one helpful action for each.
stress.why: Keeping track of your progress helps you reach your goal.

stress.title: Worry time
stress.text: Give worries 15 minutes a day. At other times, write them down for later.
stress.action: Pick a 15-minute worry time today. Use it.
stress.why: Giving worries a set time stops them filling your whole day.

stress.title: Balance check
stress.text: Study, rest, family and fun. Is one pushing out the others?
stress.action: Rate your week 1 to 5 for study, rest, people and fun.
stress.why: Keeping track of your progress helps you reach your goal.

stress.title: A bad day is information
stress.text: A bad mark does not say who you are. It shows what to fix.
stress.action: Write about one setback: what happened, what you learned, next step.
stress.why: Knowing your brain can grow helped many students do better.

stress.title: Three good things
stress.text: Writing three good things each day lifts your mood.
stress.action: Tonight, write three good things from today.
stress.why: Noticing good things and planning small joys lifts your mood.

stress.title: Your calm kit
stress.text: List what calms you. Breathing, a walk, a person, a song.
stress.action: Write your calm kit list. Keep it in your notebook.
stress.why: Same time, same place, every day: that is how habits grow.

stress.title: Who is on your team?
stress.text: Family, friends, teachers and the school counsellor can help.
stress.action: Write three people you can talk to, and how to reach them.
stress.why: People you can talk to make stress lighter.

stress.title: After Day 30
stress.text: Plans keep your calm skills going.
stress.action: Write three plans. Example: "If it feels too much, I list my top three."
stress.why: A clear "when… then…" plan makes you far more likely to act.

sleep.title: How much sleep you need
sleep.text: Teenagers need 8 to 10 hours. Most students get less.
sleep.action: Tonight, write when you go to bed and when you wake.
sleep.why: Regular sleep times and a calm bedtime help you sleep better.

sleep.title: Wake up at the same time
sleep.text: A steady wake-up time sets your body clock.
sleep.action: Choose a wake-up time. Keep it every day, even Sunday.
sleep.why: Regular sleep times and a calm bedtime help you sleep better.

sleep.title: 30 minutes to slow down
sleep.text: Your brain needs time to land. Wash, read, or talk quietly.
sleep.action: Plan three calm steps for before bed. Try them tonight.
sleep.why: Regular sleep times and a calm bedtime help you sleep better.

sleep.title: Phones and bedtime
sleep.text: A phone in bed keeps your brain awake. Charge it far away.
sleep.action: Tonight, charge your phone where you cannot reach it from bed.
sleep.why: A phone close by steals some attention, even when silent.

sleep.title: No coffee late
sleep.text: Coffee or strong tea late in the day steals sleep. Have it in the morning.
sleep.action: Pick a time today after which you have no coffee.
sleep.why: Coffee or strong tea, even 6 hours before bed, can cut your sleep.

sleep.title: List before bed
sleep.text: Write tomorrow's list before bed. Your mind can rest.
sleep.action: Tonight, write a short list for tomorrow.
sleep.why: Writing tomorrow's list helped people fall asleep faster.

sleep.title: Morning sun
sleep.text: Daylight after waking sets your body clock.
sleep.action: Get 10 minutes of daylight within an hour of waking.
sleep.why: Regular sleep times and a calm bedtime help you sleep better.

sleep.title: Bed is for sleep
sleep.text: If you study in bed, your brain learns bed means awake.
sleep.action: Today, study at a table, not on your bed.
sleep.why: Regular sleep times and a calm bedtime help you sleep better.

sleep.title: Short naps only
sleep.text: A short nap before 3 pm can help. Long naps spoil the night.
sleep.action: If you nap today, keep it under 30 minutes.
sleep.why: Regular sleep times and a calm bedtime help you sleep better.

sleep.title: Cannot sleep? Get up
sleep.text: After 20 minutes awake, get up. Do something calm. Then try again.
sleep.action: Decide what calm thing you will do if you cannot sleep.
sleep.why: Regular sleep times and a calm bedtime help you sleep better.

sleep.title: No all-night study
sleep.text: Sleep saves what you learned. Studying all night means you forget more.
sleep.action: Plan your sleep for your next busy week. No all-nighters.
sleep.why: Sleep saves what you learned. Less sleep means you forget more.

sleep.title: The weekend trap
sleep.text: Sleeping very late on weekends makes Monday feel awful.
sleep.action: Plan this weekend's sleep within an hour of school days.
sleep.why: Very different sleep times on weekends make Monday feel bad.

sleep.title: Cool, dark, quiet
sleep.text: A cool, dark, quiet room helps you sleep.
sleep.action: Make one change to your sleeping place tonight.
sleep.why: Regular sleep times and a calm bedtime help you sleep better.

sleep.title: Worries at bedtime
sleep.text: Give worries an earlier time. Write them down before bed.
sleep.action: Write your worries for 5 minutes, an hour before bed.
sleep.why: Giving worries a set time stops them filling your whole day.

sleep.title: Move by day, sleep by night
sleep.text: Moving in the day helps you sleep at night.
sleep.action: Walk, run or play for 20 minutes today.
sleep.why: Moving your body helps sleep and lowers worry.

sleep.title: Late food
sleep.text: A big meal right before bed can spoil your sleep.
sleep.action: Eat your big meal 2 to 3 hours before bed tonight.
sleep.why: Regular sleep times and a calm bedtime help you sleep better.

sleep.title: Look at your sleep notes
sleep.text: Your notes show patterns since Day 1.
sleep.action: Write your usual bedtime, wake time, and one pattern.
sleep.why: Keeping track of your progress helps you reach your goal.

sleep.title: Move bedtime slowly
sleep.text: Big changes do not last. Move bedtime 15 minutes earlier.
sleep.action: Go to bed 15 minutes earlier tonight.
sleep.why: Regular sleep times and a calm bedtime help you sleep better.

sleep.title: Sleep and mood
sleep.text: Many people feel cross or stressed after short nights.
sleep.action: Rate your mood 1 to 5. Write how many hours you slept.
sleep.why: Keeping track of your progress helps you reach your goal.

sleep.title: Exam-time sleep plan
sleep.text: In exam time, sleep matters most. Plan it now.
sleep.action: Write your exam-time plan: bedtime, calm time, no late coffee.
sleep.why: Sleep saves what you learned. Less sleep means you forget more.

sleep.title: After a late night
sleep.text: Weddings and holidays mean late nights. Wake at your usual time anyway.
sleep.action: Write your plan for the day after a late night.
sleep.why: Very different sleep times on weekends make Monday feel bad.

sleep.title: "Just one more video"
sleep.text: Videos are made to keep you watching. Plan a stop.
sleep.action: Write: "If a video ends after 10 pm, I stop."
sleep.why: A clear "when… then…" plan makes you far more likely to act.

sleep.title: When to tell someone
sleep.text: If sleep stays hard for weeks, tell a parent, teacher or nurse.
sleep.action: Write who you would talk to if sleep stays hard.
sleep.why: People you can talk to make stress lighter.

sleep.title: Your sleep card
sleep.text: Put your best sleep habits on one card.
sleep.action: Write your card: wake time, calm time, phone spot, coffee time.
sleep.why: Same time, same place, every day: that is how habits grow.

sleep.title: After Day 30
sleep.text: Plans keep your sleep rhythm going.
sleep.action: Write three "if… then…" plans for your sleep next month.
sleep.why: A clear "when… then…" plan makes you far more likely to act.

phone.title: Your phone is not the enemy
phone.text: Phones are useful. Many apps are made to grab you. Use it on purpose.
phone.action: Write how long you used your phone today, and on what.
phone.why: Keeping track of your progress helps you reach your goal.

phone.title: Out of sight
phone.text: A phone on the desk takes attention, even when quiet.
phone.action: For one study time, put your phone in another room.
phone.why: A phone close by steals some attention, even when silent.

phone.title: Fewer buzzes
phone.text: Every buzz pulls at your attention. Fewer sounds, fewer breaks.
phone.action: Turn off sounds for apps that are not real people.
phone.why: A phone close by steals some attention, even when silent.

phone.title: Make it a bit harder
phone.text: Move tempting apps off the first screen. You open them less.
phone.action: Move your two most distracting apps into a folder.
phone.why: A phone close by steals some attention, even when silent.

phone.title: Plan for the urge
phone.text: "If I reach for my phone, I take one breath and keep going."
phone.action: Write one "if… then…" plan for phone urges. Use it today.
phone.why: A clear "when… then…" plan makes you far more likely to act.

phone.title: Phone-free mornings
phone.text: Messages first thing make you rush. Start the day calm.
phone.action: Tomorrow, wait 20 minutes after waking before you check your phone.
phone.why: Same time, same place, every day: that is how habits grow.

phone.title: Swap, do not just stop
phone.text: If you stop scrolling with nothing to do, the urge comes back.
phone.action: Write three things to do instead of scrolling when bored.
phone.why: A clear "when… then…" plan makes you far more likely to act.

phone.title: Set a time limit
phone.text: A limit makes you stop and choose.
phone.action: Set a daily limit for your most-used app.
phone.why: A phone close by steals some attention, even when silent.

phone.title: Grey screen test
phone.text: A grey screen makes colourful apps less tempting.
phone.action: Turn your screen grey for one day. Notice the change.
phone.why: A phone close by steals some attention, even when silent.

phone.title: Clean your feed
phone.text: Some accounts make you feel worse. You can mute them.
phone.action: Mute five accounts or groups that make you feel bad.
phone.why: Checking a bad thought and finding a fairer one helps you.

phone.title: Phone-free people time
phone.text: A phone on the table takes away from talking.
phone.action: Have one meal or coffee time today with no phone.
phone.why: A phone close by steals some attention, even when silent.

phone.title: Park your phone at night
phone.text: A phone in bed pushes sleep later.
phone.action: Tonight, charge your phone away from your bed.
phone.why: Regular sleep times and a calm bedtime help you sleep better.

phone.title: Check at set times
phone.text: Checking all day breaks your day into pieces.
phone.action: Pick three times today to check messages.
phone.why: Short study times with planned breaks keep your mind fresh.

phone.title: "I will miss something!"
phone.text: It feels true. It is rarely true. Messages wait.
phone.action: Write: "Important messages will still be there in 25 minutes."
phone.why: Checking a bad thought and finding a fairer one helps you.

phone.title: Study mode
phone.text: Turn on silent or flight mode while you study. 4 works offline.
phone.action: Turn on flight mode for one study block.
phone.why: A phone close by steals some attention, even when silent.

phone.title: Tell your friends
phone.text: Tell friends when you are studying. They will not wait for fast replies.
phone.action: Tell your group chat when you will be offline today.
phone.why: Students who set their own small deadlines did better.

phone.title: Count the urges
phone.text: When do you want your phone? Bored? Stuck? Worried?
phone.action: Count your phone urges in one study time. Note why.
phone.why: Keeping track of your progress helps you reach your goal.

phone.title: Slip without a spiral
phone.text: Lost an evening to your phone? It happens. Be kind. Try again.
phone.action: If you slip, write one kind sentence and one plan for tomorrow.
phone.why: Students who forgave themselves put things off less next time.

phone.title: Screens off time
phone.text: Pick a time each evening when screens go off.
phone.action: Choose a screens-off time tonight. Keep it.
phone.why: Regular sleep times and a calm bedtime help you sleep better.

phone.title: Make your phone your helper
phone.text: Use it for good: study timer, reminders, alarm.
phone.action: Set two reminders: "start studying" and "get ready for bed".
phone.why: A clear "when… then…" plan makes you far more likely to act.

phone.title: Busy group chats
phone.text: Mute busy groups. Check them at set times.
phone.action: Mute one busy group chat today.
phone.why: A phone close by steals some attention, even when silent.

phone.title: Five minutes of nothing
phone.text: Sitting with your thoughts is hard. Practice makes slow work easier.
phone.action: Sit 5 minutes with no phone and no music. Notice what happens.
phone.why: Practising quiet time helps you handle slow, dull work.

phone.title: Compare with Day 1
phone.text: Look at your phone time now. What changed?
phone.action: Write your phone time now and one thing that helped.
phone.why: Keeping track of your progress helps you reach your goal.

phone.title: Your phone rules
phone.text: Turn what worked into a few simple rules.
phone.action: Write three phone rules, like "phone stays away while I study".
phone.why: Same time, same place, every day: that is how habits grow.

phone.title: After Day 30
phone.text: Plans keep your balance.
phone.action: Write three "if… then…" plans for your phone next month.
phone.why: A clear "when… then…" plan makes you far more likely to act.

motivation.title: Doing comes first
motivation.text: We wait to feel like it. But the feeling comes after we start.
motivation.action: Pick one goal. Do a 2-minute version today.
motivation.why: Same time, same place, every day: that is how habits grow.

motivation.title: Find your reason
motivation.text: Link school to what you care about: a job, your family, your village.
motivation.action: Write two sentences: how can one subject help you or others?
motivation.why: You try harder when you see why it matters to you.

motivation.title: Your choice
motivation.text: Feeling in charge helps. Even choosing the first task helps.
motivation.action: Today, choose the order of your tasks yourself.
motivation.why: You try harder when you see why it matters to you.

motivation.title: Your brain can grow
motivation.text: Skills grow with effort, good methods and help.
motivation.action: Write about one skill you got better at by practice.
motivation.why: Knowing your brain can grow helped many students do better.

motivation.title: Count small wins
motivation.text: Small progress keeps you going. Write it down.
motivation.action: Write three small wins from today.
motivation.why: Keeping track of your progress helps you reach your goal.

motivation.title: Wish, picture, problem, plan
motivation.text: Picture your goal. Picture what may stop you. Plan for it.
motivation.action: For one goal, write: wish, best result, problem, plan.
motivation.why: Thinking about the problem before it comes helps you beat it. It was tested with high school students.

motivation.title: Join it to a habit
motivation.text: "After dinner, I read my notes for 10 minutes."
motivation.action: Write one "after… I will…" sentence. Try it today.
motivation.why: A clear "when… then…" plan makes you far more likely to act.

motivation.title: Better together
motivation.text: Studying with a friend makes it less lonely.
motivation.action: Ask one friend to study with you this week.
motivation.why: People you can talk to make stress lighter.

motivation.title: "Not yet"
motivation.text: "I am bad at maths" shuts the door. "Not yet" keeps it open.
motivation.action: Change one "I can't" into "I can't yet. I can try…"
motivation.why: Knowing your brain can grow helped many students do better.

motivation.title: Why it matters to you
motivation.text: How could today's topic help in real life? On the farm? At home?
motivation.action: Write a few lines: how is today's topic useful in your life?
motivation.why: You try harder when you see why it matters to you.

motivation.title: Rewards that help
motivation.text: A small treat after studying makes starting easier.
motivation.action: Pick a small treat for after one study task today.
motivation.why: Pairing a dull task with something you enjoy makes it easier to do.

motivation.title: No-energy days
motivation.text: Some days you will not feel it. Do 10 minutes anyway.
motivation.action: Today, do just 10 minutes of something on your list.
motivation.why: Short study times with planned breaks keep your mind fresh.

motivation.title: Big goal, small steps
motivation.text: Link your matric goal to this week's small steps.
motivation.action: Write one big goal. Write three steps for this week.
motivation.why: Small, clear steps are easier to start. Each one done gives you hope.

motivation.title: See how you grew
motivation.text: Seeing your skills grow gives you energy.
motivation.action: Compare something you can do now with a month ago.
motivation.why: You try harder when you see why it matters to you.

motivation.title: Mistakes teach
motivation.text: Every mistake shows what to practise next.
motivation.action: Look at one mistake. Write what it teaches you.
motivation.why: Knowing your brain can grow helped many students do better.

motivation.title: Fuel your body
motivation.text: Low energy can feel like no motivation. Sleep, food and water matter.
motivation.action: Fix one basic today: sleep, water, food or a walk.
motivation.why: Moving your body helps sleep and lowers worry.

motivation.title: Even great people struggled
motivation.text: Famous scientists failed many times before they succeeded.
motivation.action: Think of someone you admire who struggled first.
motivation.why: Learning that great scientists struggled helped students try harder.

motivation.title: Bigger than you
motivation.text: Learning can help others: your family, your village, your country.
motivation.action: Write one way your learning could help others one day.
motivation.why: You try harder when you see why it matters to you.

motivation.title: What matters most to you
motivation.text: Writing about what you value lowers stress.
motivation.action: Write for 5 minutes about something that really matters to you.
motivation.why: Writing about what matters to you can lower stress.

motivation.title: Plan for low days
motivation.text: Low days will come. Plan a small version now.
motivation.action: Write: "If I feel low, I will do 10 minutes of…"
motivation.why: A clear "when… then…" plan makes you far more likely to act.

motivation.title: Celebrate
motivation.text: You are three weeks in. Be proud of your effort.
motivation.action: Celebrate in a small way. Write what you are proud of.
motivation.why: Noticing good things and planning small joys lifts your mood.

motivation.title: Help someone else
motivation.text: Students who gave study tips to younger students did better too.
motivation.action: Share one study tip with a brother, sister or classmate.
motivation.why: Students who gave study tips to others did better themselves.

motivation.title: Look back
motivation.text: What gave you energy these weeks? What took it away?
motivation.action: Write two things that helped and one that drained you.
motivation.why: Keeping track of your progress helps you reach your goal.

motivation.title: Your drive kit
motivation.text: Keep your best tools in one place: your reason, small steps, rewards.
motivation.action: Write your list of drive tools in your notebook.
motivation.why: Same time, same place, every day: that is how habits grow.

motivation.title: After Day 30
motivation.text: Plans keep you going.
motivation.action: Write three "if… then…" plans for next month.
motivation.why: A clear "when… then…" plan makes you far more likely to act.

caffeine_timing.why: Coffee or strong tea, even 6 hours before bed, can cut your sleep.

sleep_memory.why: Sleep saves what you learned. Less sleep means you forget more.

social_jetlag.why: Very different sleep times on weekends make Monday feel bad.
